x: Another of our quieter stalwarts Paul Pringle, is also showing great improvements of late (see Finchley 20m result) and proving a great 'back up' man in the longer events.

Personal bests also went to Clive Shippen and Paul Pringle, the latter taking 30 mins(!) off his previous time. For good measure Pat O'Connor also won the Middlesex individual championship held in conjunction and then completed the day by winning a raffle prize of a bottle of sherry, which was quick…
This was the half way mark (51:34) and supporting our key men were Clive Shippen (56:18), Brian Joines (60:49), Paul Pringle (60:49) and Jack Baker (62:03).
Two inveterate Belgrave mudlarks took part in this year's wallow. Don Bonser covered the course in 1hr. 59m. 40s. in 73rd place, and Paul Pringle clocked 2hrs. 09m. 05s in 86th.

Paul Pringle's time is his best ever for a marathon whilst George Piddington's run gained him 8th place in the Hampshire Championship held in conjunction.
Paul Pringle finished 172nd in 2:57:15, Don Bonsor 213th in 3:19:22 and George Piddington, taking a little light relief from his job as Belgrave's Press Secretary, 219th in 3:24:14.
The indefatigable Paul Pringle was our next man home, a minute or so ahead of John Davis, of 1:52.8 880yds/4:10.6 mile fame some 17 years ago and here making his debut at the marathon.
Left to right - Stuart Barrett, Paul Williamson, John Flynn (obscured), Paul Pringle and Dave Davies.

This year's race in May took place on a very hot day when only the first 21 beat 3 hours. Paul Pringle's 2:53:58 (16th) was excellent. George (52nd) reached the finish in 3:56:47 having taken 68 minutes for the last six miles!

Our other starter, Paul Pringle, had to retire before the finish, a great pity as we know how hard and conscientiously he trains. Congratulations to Bill and Glenn, to run to Brighton is a feather in anybody's cap.
It was surprising that he didn't gain a handicap award but Paul Pringle and Charlie Henn chose this day also to run exceptionally well and thwarted him.
What's wrong with the intellectual talents of Paul Pringle and why can't Eddie Thorp or Alan Black display their talents of leadership? Remember - you've got a bloody good Vice-Captain.

PAUL PRINGLE, who trains so conscientiously and who failed to finish last year, completed the journey in 7 hours 34 mins 15 seconds. Although outside second-class standard time it earned him a certificate for finishing within the time limit.
A Belgrave trio of Bill Weller (3:04:46), Lionel Mann (3:19:06) and Paul Pringle (3:25:05) placed 5th, 13th and 19th to gain the third team prizes with 37 points.

A little way back John Davies and Paul Pringle were keeping each other company, and John Baker and Dave Drake were steadily plodding away. By 20 km positions were much the same with the effects of the heat beginning to show.
Eddie Thorp slipped back after a fast start but was fighting well, having been passed by Paul Pringle but keeping ahead of the rest of the Belgrave pack led by Mr.
Paul Pringle, just home from holiday in Jugoslavia (where he enjoyed a daily run) was 49th in 2:56:25, and hoping to do a steady ten miles the following day.
It was good to see another Davies family supporting the lads, Stan (up to town from Suffolk) and Dai. Paul Pringle was unlucky to finish a few seconds over the 3 hours mark.
Paul Pringle at 125th was pleased to get near the 3 hour barrier with 3:00:59, whilst Doug Maughan and Geoff Pearson ran to 3:10:47 and 3:32:31 respectively for their 153rd and 181st places.

Brew and John Davies occupy 548th and 549th placings - separated by two seconds (but over different courses). Paul Pringle is on the right side of the three hours mark in 651st (689 beat three hours).

Veteran (40+) Paul Pringle chose what many regard as the toughest of them all, the Isle of Wight to do 3:11.21 for 1089th placing. Another of our "evergreen" runners, Geoff Pearson (now 60+) went to W.Berlin for the World Vets.
